tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Local sections, Euclidean form]

↗ lem:surjection-splits

Let $E, E'$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let $f : E \to E'$ be $C^\infty $ at $a$, and suppose $df_a$ is surjective. Then there is a map $\sigma : E' \to E$, $C^\infty $ at $f(a)$, with $\sigma (f(a)) = a$ and $f(\sigma (y)) = y$ for every $y$ near $f(a)$.

Proof

↗ lem:surjection-splits Let $P : E \to \ker df_a$ be a continuous linear projection and set $G(x) = (f(x), P(x))$, a map $E \to E' \times \ker df_a$ which is $C^\infty $ at $a$. Its differential at $a$ is $v \mapsto (df_a v, Pv)$, which is a linear isomorphism by Lemma 4. By the inverse function theorem $G$ has a local inverse $G^{-1}$ defined near $G(a)$, which is $C^\infty $ at $G(a)$ and satisfies $G^{-1}(G(a)) = a$ and $G(G^{-1}(z)) = z$ for $z$ near $G(a)$.

Set $\sigma (y) = G^{-1}(y, P(a))$. Then $\sigma $ is $C^\infty $ at $f(a)$, being $G^{-1}$ composed with the affine map $y \mapsto (y, P(a))$, which sends $f(a)$ to $G(a)$. Also $\sigma (f(a)) = G^{-1}(G(a)) = a$. Finally, $y \mapsto (y, P(a))$ is continuous and sends $f(a)$ to $G(a)$, so for $y$ near $f(a)$ we have $G(G^{-1}(y, P(a))) = (y, P(a))$; taking first components gives $f(\sigma (y)) = y$.

□

The same map $G$ carries more information than the local section extracted from it: because its first component is literally $f$, it is a chart in which the level sets of $f$ become affine slices. That is the local model for the regular level set theorem (Corollary 12), and it is recorded separately here.
